headline: High: Replit Agent can write and execute in a persistent workspace while Airflow can egress broadly, creating dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflict, and unverified downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no direct ingest channel from B, but B can write Repl workspace files and A can interact with APIs; if A consumes files or outputs from B in a shared workspace, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance mechanism, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF B writes attacker-controlled instructions into a workspace file that A later reads
IF A is configured to parse B-produced text as trusted directives
mitigations: Separate workspaces so A never reads B-written files
Require explicit allowlists for any file A ingests
Add provenance tags to B outputs before A consumes them
Disable automatic file-based instruction ingestion
requires-engineering: add a sanitizer/provenance gate between B and A

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad filesystem/network access; A has broad network egress and can call external APIs. If B passes sensitive workspace content into A, A can transmit it outward. This is a default-dangerous exfiltration pathway, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF B loads secrets or deployment files into prompts or artifacts that A can access
IF A sends those artifacts to external APIs or services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files
Restrict A to non-sensitive datasets only
Turn off A network egress for sensitive runs
Rotate any secrets exposed in shared workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before A egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl filesystem; A is a data orchestrator with broad egress. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other without locking. The shared-state model makes this a default high-risk conflict.
conditions: IF A and B target the same repository or workspace
IF B commits or rewrites files while A is also producing artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a lock file around git operations
Review diffs before any commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write serialization

D_cascading_error.rationale: B can act on A-generated artifacts inside a Repl, and A can produce outputs that B may treat as operational inputs. There is no documented verification loop between them, so A's mistakes can cascade into B's file edits or deployments. The blast radius is meaningful but not inherently irreversible in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF B uses A's outputs as authoritative without review
IF B executes shell or git actions based on A-produced text
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B acts
Add a verification checklist for B
Limit B to dry-run mode for A-derived tasks
Log A-to-B handoffs for audit
requires-engineering: add schema validation for A outputs

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches secrets and deployment configuration in a Replit-managed cloud environment, while A has broad network egress. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed in B's workspace and then processed by A, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not prove a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data or EU PII is stored in B's Repl workspace
IF A processes that data through external network calls without a DPA or residency control
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Confirm data-processing agreements before use
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Restrict A to approved regions/services
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing and retention controls
